title: Three-body potentials with ireset 1, more than 9 angles
purpose: Exercises the three-body input of the `epsr` engine [@soper1996,@soper2005,@epsrmanual] at its limits: a group with more angles than the 9 allowed, and a complete potential reset (`ireset 1`) in the same run.
system: The EPSR-test system: a liquid mixture of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO, (CH3)2SO) and 400 water molecules (DMSO mole fraction 1/3; 3200 atoms) at 300 K in a cubic box of side 33.12 Å (atomic number density 0.0881 atoms/Å³). DMSO uses EPSR's Lennard-Jones + Coulomb reference potential with methyl rotational groups; water uses SPC/E Lennard-Jones and charge parameters [@berendsen1987] with EPSR's flexible intramolecular geometry (O-H 0.976 Å). The empirical potential is refined against three neutron diffraction data sets of deuterated DMSO in D2O, in null-scattering H2O/D2O and in H2O (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), the isotope-substitution approach of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992]. A `tb A1 A2 A3 amp awidth rwidth rmax12 rmax32 s12 s23 s13 ang1 amp1 ...` line in the `.pcof` adds an angular energy `amp*ampN*0.5*((cos theta - cosN)/awidth)²` to every triplet A1-A2-A3 (A2 the centre) within the distance limits, for the requested angle N closest to theta; the flags select same or different molecules. Groups: water O1-H1···O1 with 10 angle/amplitude pairs (180° to 135°) plus an odd trailing word, and intramolecular DMSO O-S-C (106°).
inputs: EPSR-test with the two `tb` lines appended to the `.pcof`; `ireset 1` in the `.EPSR.inp` (reset to 0 on saving, so pass 2 runs with `ireset 0`). `commands.txt`: `epsr 200DMSO400Water.EPSR.inp`, `repeat 2`.
verification: `(nwords-12)/2 = 10` angles are capped at 9. Pass 2 reads back the `.pcof` written by pass 1, with the altered `tb` values described below, so both the reset path and the re-read of the program's own output are compared.
notes: Fortran quirk reproduced: with `ireset 1` the default pair potentials reset `nsymbol`, so the `tb` symbols are no longer counted; when the `ndata` line is processed the `tb` values are not moved and at save time the groups are not re-read: the in-memory values are written (width 1.0 rad -> `57.30`, cosines -> angles such as `-57.30`), and pass 2 uses them.
